principle: each visual attribute should have one dominant reference authority; style target never owns identity geometry or garment architecture unless explicitly authorized.

identity_A_wardrobe_B.use_when: The user authorizes wardrobe redesign and the current brief explicitly assigns Image B as a clothing-design reference.
identity_A_wardrobe_B.brief_precedence: Explicit adaptation controls the allowed wardrobe changes, accessory limits, pose and background. Visible body or hairstyle requirements from the user remain authoritative; an unseen body cannot be measured from a portrait.
prompt_binding: Image A is the sole source of the character's face, apparent age, expression, hair color and hairstyle, except changes explicitly authorized in this brief.

Image B supplies only the clothing construction, palette, material relationships and selected accessories named in the wardrobe brief. Do not copy B's face, body proportions, hair, forehead marks or unassigned head ornaments.
The explicit wardrobe adaptation takes precedence over conflicting clothing details in either image. Follow the specified pose and background rather than automatically inheriting B's presentation.
review: Check identity and hair against A separately from costume construction against B.
Check B-only face, hair, forehead and body traits for unwanted transfer; absence of one obvious trait does not prove identity preservation.
Check the final accessory count and ornament density against the adaptation brief; B can introduce extra detail despite role text.
Record B as an actual generation input, not evaluation-only. Do not label the result a pure prompt-only improvement.

A.rule: decompose channels; visible identity/costume may be strong, unseen structure remains conservative completion; style channels may be strong.
